Filters
Learning Level (learn more)
Topics

Beginner For those learning about a topic for the first time or looking to gain foundational knowledge before starting a project. For these presentations, you will walk away with a conceptual understanding, knowledge of basic tools, and/or the first steps required to try it out.

Intermediate Sessions for those actively working with the technology daily and who want to improve their efficiency, testing, and/or application of best practices. In these sessions, you may learn concrete code examples, testing strategies, common pitfalls, and/or methods to solve medium-complexity problems.

Advanced For the attendees who are actively designing or leading projects with a particular technology and want to understand complex trade-offs, scalability, and integration challenges. These sessions may allow you to gain unique, production-tested insights, architectural patterns, performance optimization tips, and/or analysis of design trade-offs.

AI writes most of the code now, so the hard part of engineering has moved from authoring to the part we’re worse at - verifying. With the incentives all pushing toward shipping faster and faster - the rational move is to skim the diff, click through a little manual QA, and ship on vibes.

Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop

Avoiding Prompt Debt & Other Context Failures

As agents evolve, prompts get unruly. Edge cases are patched with one-line hotfixes, or with stacked instructions of escalating severity when an issue proves stubborn. Over time, those instructions pile up into a brittle artifact, overfit to an aging model.
